paper.title_en: Lifetime measurements in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts></math>: Investigation of seniority conservation in the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></math> isotones
paper.abstract_en: Excited states in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts></math> have been populated in fusion-evaporation reactions and their lifetimes have been measured using the fast-timing technique with a setup consisting of LaBr scintillators and high-purity germanium detectors. The resulting lifetimes are used to calculate reduced quadrupole transition probabilities and discussed within the context of seniority conservation in the <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbital. In contrast to the latest experimental findings, the new experimental data indicate that seniority symmetry is partially conserved in the midshell nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.
